# sca security_key

[← Command reference](../commands.md)

`<sca_options>` are the [global options](../commands.md#global-options).

```text
The sca security key command help

The security key command is used for managing cryptographic token storage devices
- devices that securely store and utilize cryptographic information including
private keys and certificates.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] security_key [<security_key_options>] <security_key_command>

security_key_options:

  -h, --help                    - display security key command help and exit

The security key command is one of the following:

  get_crt   - retrieving certificate for the given entity from a security key
  id        - retrieving ids of the currently inserted security key
  init      - first time initialization of security_key
  unblock_pin - unblock a blocked pin with the stored puk, and update the pin file
  upload    - upload security document to security key
  wait_for  - awaits for specific security key connection
```

**See also**

```text
type sca security_key <subcommand> --help for further information on each of the
security key related commands.
```

### Choosing a key: `--device SERIAL`

Every `security_key` subcommand accepts `--device SERIAL`, the YubiKey's hardware serial as printed by `sca security_key id` (or `ykman list --serials`). The serial is passed on to the tools: `yubico-piv-tool` is pointed at that key's reader, and `pkcs11-tool` at its `YubiKey PIV #<serial>` token.

- `info` and `verify`: with one key attached, `--device` is optional and nothing changes. With more than one attached and no `--device`, the command prints the attached serials and exits non-zero rather than pick one.
- `get_crt`, `init`, `unblock_pin`, `upload` and `wait_for`: these wait for the entity's configured key (`<entity>_security_key_id`). `--device` waits for the named key instead, which is how a second (backup) key of the same entity is reached. If no key is configured and more than one is attached, they refuse in the same way.
- `id`: lists only the named key, and fails if it is not attached.

```bash
sca security_key id                         # 12345678 0
                                            # 87654321 1
sca security_key info --device 87654321
sca security_key upload --device 87654321 subca crt
```

If one attached reader's name is contained in another's, `yubico-piv-tool` cannot tell those two keys apart. In that case `sca` refuses and asks you to attach only the key you want to use.

**Subcommands**

- [get_crt](#sca-security_key-get_crt) - retrieving certificate for the given entity from a security key
- [id](#sca-security_key-id) - retrieving ids of the currently inserted security key
- [info](#sca-security_key-info)
- [init](#sca-security_key-init) - first time initialization of security_key
- [unblock_pin](#sca-security_key-unblock_pin) - unblock a blocked pin with the stored puk, and update the pin file
- [upload](#sca-security_key-upload) - upload security document to security key
- [verify](#sca-security_key-verify)
- [wait_for](#sca-security_key-wait_for) - awaits for specific security key connection

## sca security_key get_crt

```text
The security key get certificate command help

The security key get certificate command is used for retrieving certificate for
the given entity from a security key and according to the configuration.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] security_key [<security_key_options>] get_crt [<get_crt_options>]

security_key_options:

  -h, --help                    - display security key command help and exit

get_crt_options:

  -h, --help                - print this help
  --device SERIAL           - use the security key with this serial instead of
                              the one configured for the entity. needed to
                              reach a second (backup) key of the same entity.
```

**Example:**
```bash
# Get sub-CA certificate from YubiKey
sca security_key get_crt subca
```

## sca security_key id

```text
The security key id command help

The security key id command is used for retrieving ids of the currently inserted
cryptographic token secure storage devices.

A security key id is the first 6 hexadecimal numbers of the token secure storage
device serial number, separated by dash '-' character.

The opensc card reader number associated with the security key is printed along
with the security key id with white space as a separator.

In case there are more than one security keys connected to the computer, they
will all be displayed one on each line.

In case there are no security keys connected to the system, dash sign is
displayed for both security key id and the card reader number.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] security_key [<security_key_options>] id [<id_options>]

security_key_options:

  -h, --help                    - display security key command help and exit

id_options:

  -h, --help                - print this help
  -t, --security-key-type   - retrieve security keys only for security keys of
                              specified type. currently supported type is
                              yubikey only.
  --device SERIAL           - list only the security key with this serial, and
                              exit with an error if it is not attached.
```

Useful for identifying which key is inserted when you have multiple YubiKeys: each attached key is printed on its own line as `<serial> <reader number>`.

## sca security_key info

```text
The security key info command help

The security key info command displays the status of all PIV slots on a connected
YubiKey, including certificate details and private key presence.

For each populated slot, it shows the certificate subject, expiration date, and
whether a private key is present. This is useful for verifying YubiKey contents
and diagnosing issues with key storage.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] security_key [<security_key_options>] info [<info_options>]

security_key_options:

  -h, --help                    - display security key command help and exit

info_options:

  -h, --help                - print this help
  --device SERIAL           - act on the security key with this serial. when
                              more than one key is attached, it is required:
                              the command lists the attached serials and
                              exits rather than pick one.
```

**Example output:**
```
YubiKey PIV Slot Information
============================

Slot 9c (Digital Signature):
  Subject:   MyCompany SubCA - admin
  Expires:   Jan 21 19:16:13 2036 GMT
  Algorithm: rsaEncryption

Slot 82 (Retired Key 1 (CA)):
  Subject:   MyCompany CA
  Expires:   Jan 21 19:44:49 2036 GMT
  Algorithm: rsaEncryption
```

## sca security_key init

```text
The security key init command help

The security key init command is used for first time initialization of the
currently inserted cryptographic token secure storage device as well as for
security key access keys.

A security key initialization consists of setting the three security key access
keys: pin, puk and the management key. The passwords are randomly generated and
saved to the keys file-system.

You should write down the pin and remember the pin. It's 6 digits that you will
need to use to access the keys stored on the token device.

It is good to have the management key somewhere on paper as well although it is
best used only in air-gapped environment where it's safe to attach the keys
file-system.

Rolling (assigning new values to) the access keys is also performed by this
command when ran with appropriate parameters.

IMPORTANT NOTE: this command shall be run in an air-gapped (offline,
disconnected from the internet) environment.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] security_key [<security_key_options>] init [<init_options>] <entity>

security_key_options:

  -h, --help                    - display security key command help and exit

init_options:

  -h, --help      - print this help
  -r, --roll-keys - change security key access keys (pin/puk/management key) by
                    setting the new ones randomly generated
  --device SERIAL - use the security key with this serial instead of the one
                    configured for the entity. needed to reach a second
                    (backup) key of the same entity.

The entity parameter is the type of the entity for which we want to initialize
the security key for. The sca configuration file assigns a cryptographic token
storage device (a security key) to each of the declared default entity types
(ca, subca, user, service, host). The related setting name is:
<entity>_security_key_id.
```

**What it does:**
- Generates a new random management key, PIN and PUK, and sets them on the key
  (replacing the factory defaults, or the current values with `--roll-keys`)
- Stores them in `~/.sca/keys/<ca>/<subca>/private/` (created if missing,
  mode 0700) as `<prefix>yubikey-{key,pin,puk}.txt`, mode 0600. With
  `--roll-keys` the previous files are kept as `*.bak`
- If setting a value fails, the files still match what is on the key: when
  nothing changed they are left as they were; when only part changed, they
  record the new values for what changed, and the error says which ones

**Important:** Save the generated credentials! You'll need the PUK if you forget your PIN.

## sca security_key unblock_pin

```text
The security key unblock_pin command help

The security key unblock_pin command recovers a PIV pin that is blocked after
too many wrong attempts, using the puk sca stored when the security key was
initialized, and keeps sca's pin file in step with the key.

By default a new random pin is set on the key and, once the key has taken it,
written to the entity's pin file (mode 0600). With --keep-pin the pin already
in the pin file is set again instead, and the file is not changed.

The puk is tried once only. If the puk file is missing, or the key refuses the
puk, the command stops, leaves the pin file as it was, and says how many puk
retries remain. A blocked puk leaves only a reset of the PIV application, which
destroys its keys; see docs/yubikey.md.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] security_key [<security_key_options>] unblock_pin [<unblock_pin_options>] <entity>

security_key_options:

  -h, --help                    - display security key command help and exit

unblock_pin_options:

  -h, --help      - print this help
  -k, --keep-pin  - set the pin already in the pin file again, rather than a
                    new random one
  --device SERIAL - use the security key with this serial instead of the one
                    configured for the entity. needed to reach a second
                    (backup) key of the same entity.

entity is one of: ca, subca, user, service, host
```

**What it does:**
- Reads the PUK from `<prefix>yubikey-puk.txt` and runs `yubico-piv-tool -a unblock-pin` on the entity's key
- By default sets a new random PIN and, once the key has taken it, writes it to `<prefix>yubikey-pin.txt` (mode 0600)
- `-k`, `--keep-pin`: set the PIN already in the PIN file again; the file is not changed
- The PUK is tried once only. If the PUK file is missing, or the key refuses the PUK, it stops with the PIN file unchanged and says how many PUK retries remain. A blocked PUK leaves only a [PIV reset](../yubikey.md#reset-piv-emergency), which destroys the keys on it

**Example:**
```bash
sca security_key verify subca         # FAILED ... PIN error (wrong PIN or PIN blocked)
sca security_key unblock_pin subca
sca security_key verify subca         # SUCCESS
```

## sca security_key upload

```text
The security key upload command help

The security key upload command is used for uploading a security document into a
cryptographic token secure storage device.

The security documents that are stored in security keys include private keys and
certificates. Each security key device can hold one or more private key - certificate
pairs. For example, yubikey 4 can keep 25 such pairs.

Unless the force flag had been specified, the upload will fail in case the
target security key storage slot has been already occupied by certificate/key.
Forcing replacing the current values in the security key storage slot.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] security_key [<security_key_options>] upload [<upload_options>] <entity> <document>

security_key_options:

  -h, --help                    - display security key command help and exit

upload_options:

  -h, --help      - print this help
  -f, --force     - force will replace any existing key or certificate in the
                    target security key storage slot.
  --device SERIAL - use the security key with this serial instead of the one
                    configured for the entity. needed to reach a second
                    (backup) key of the same entity.

entity may be either ca, subca, user, host or service
document may be either crt (for certificate) or key (for private key)
```

Each call uploads one document, so uploading both the certificate and the private key takes two calls.

The target slot is derived from the entity's `pkcs11_id` setting (e.g. `02` → slot 9c for the sub-CA default, `05` → slot 82 for the CA default). See [PIV Slots](../yubikey.md#piv-slots).

**Example:**
```bash
# Upload sub-CA certificate and private key to YubiKey
sca security_key upload subca crt
sca security_key upload subca key
```

After upload, the private key on disk can be securely deleted - all signing operations will use the YubiKey.

## sca security_key verify

```text
The security key verify command help

The security key verify command tests whether a private key is present and
functional on the YubiKey for a given entity. It does this by attempting to
sign test data with the key.

This is the only reliable way to detect private key presence, as tools like
ykman and yubico-piv-tool may incorrectly report keys as missing due to
display bugs.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] security_key [<security_key_options>] verify [<verify_options>] <entity>

security_key_options:

  -h, --help                    - display security key command help and exit

verify_options:

  -h, --help                - print this help
  --device SERIAL           - act on the security key with this serial. when
                              more than one key is attached, it is required:
                              the command lists the attached serials and
                              exits rather than pick one.

entity is one of: ca, subca, user, service, host
```

**Example:**
```bash
# Verify sub-CA private key on YubiKey
sca security_key verify subca

# Verify CA private key (if stored on YubiKey)
sca security_key verify ca
```

This is the most reliable way to confirm a key exists, as tools like `ykman piv info` may incorrectly report "Private key: Not present" even when keys are working.

The ykcs11 module path comes from the `ykcs11_module` config setting. If that file doesn't exist, common install locations are searched before failing. See [YubiKey Setup](../yubikey.md#verify-private-key-presence).

## sca security_key wait_for

```text
The security key wait for command help

The security key wait for command is used for pausing execution of a program and
prompting a user to insert particular security key device.

A security key wait for is used internally by sca and may be useful in custom
tools for management of security keys.

The last output line is the number of the smart card reader through in which
the awaited security key resides.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] security_key [<security_key_options>] wait_for [<wait_for_options>] <entity>

security_key_options:

  -h, --help                    - display security key command help and exit

wait_for_options:

  -h, --help      - print this help
  --device SERIAL - use the security key with this serial instead of the one
                    configured for the entity. needed to reach a second
                    (backup) key of the same entity.
```

The key is identified by the serial configured in `<entity>_security_key_id`, or the one given with `--device`. Useful in scripts.

**Example:**
```bash
# Wait for the sub-CA's configured YubiKey
sca security_key wait_for subca

# Wait for the sub-CA's backup YubiKey, serial 12345678
sca security_key wait_for --device 12345678 subca
```
